result.topic_en: Euler reduces Fermat's equation for cubes to a system of conditions in auxiliary quantities seeking a contradiction, then states an unproved theorem that no rational quantities have sum times product equal to unity, and notes that Fermat's theorem for cubes would follow from it.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 235
$c^{2\lambda}-4a^\lambda b^\lambda=(a^\lambda-b^\lambda)^2=\square$,
ideoque pro $ab$ posito $d$, talis formula $c^{2\lambda}-4d^\lambda$ deberet esse quadratum, cujus igitur impossibilitatem ostendi oportet, praeter casus $\lambda=1$ et $\lambda=2$.
Corollarium. Simili modo ex formula $b^\lambda=c^\lambda-a^\lambda$ deducitur
$b^{2\lambda}+4c^\lambda a^\lambda=(c^\lambda+a^\lambda)^2=\square$,
quin etiam $a^{2\lambda}+4c^\lambda b^\lambda=\square$, quae ergo formulae etiam sunt impossibiles. Demonstratio pro casu saltem $\lambda=3$ ita tentetur: Cum sit $a^3+b^3=c^3$, erit $(a+b)(aa-ab+bb)=c^3$, quos factores ut primos inter se spectemus, cum casus, quo divisorem communem habent 3, nullam novam difficultatem implicet. Sit igitur uterque cubus $a+b=p^3$ et $aa-ab+bb=P^3$, fietque $c=Pp$; tum vero erit $p^6-P^3=3ab$, deinde ob $b^3=c^3-a^3=(c-a)(cc+ac+aa)$,
fiat iterum $c-a=q^3$ et $cc+ac+aa=Q^3$, fietque $b=Qq$ et $Q^3-q^6=3ac$,
denique ob $a^3=c^3-b^3=(c-b)(cc+bc+bb)$ sit $c-b=r^3$ et $cc+bc+bb=R^3$ unde $a=Rr$ et $R^3-r^6=3bc$.
Introductis igitur litteris $p$, $q$, $r$ et $P$, $Q$, $R$, ob $c=Pp$, $b=Qq$ et $a=Rr$, sequentes conditiones sunt adimplendae:
I. $p^3=Rr+Qq$, II. $q^3=Pp-Rr$, III. $r^3=Pp-Qq$,
IV. $P^3=RRrr-RrQq+QQqq$, V. $Q^3=PPpp+PpRr+RRrr$, VI. $R^3=PPpp+PpQq+QQqq$,
quibus praeterea adjungere licet
VII. $p^6-P^3=3QqRr$, VIII. $Q^3-q^6=3PpRr$, IX. $R^3-r^6=3PpQq$.
Denique etiam notasse juvabit $Q^3-P^3=(c-b)(a+c-b)=(Pp+Qq)(Rr+Pp-Qq)$. Totum ergo negotium huc redit, ut in his conditionibus contradictio detegatur.
p. 113.
6.
Theorema demonstrandum. Non dantur plures quantitates rationales veluti $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, etc. quarum summa $A+B+C+D$ etc. per productum $ABCD$ etc. multiplicata producat unitatem. Sive si hoc signum $\neq$ denotet impossibilitatem aequalitatis, theorema hoc complectitur sequentes formas:
I. $AB(A+B)\neq1$, II. $ABC(A+B+C)\neq1$, III. $ABCD(A+B+C+D)\neq1$, etc.
Hae formae etiam ita exhiberi possunt
I. $A+B\neq\frac{1}{AB}$, II. $A+B+C\neq\frac{1}{ABC}$, III. $A+B+C+D\neq\frac{1}{ABCD}$, etc.
Hinc si postremae formulae fractae referantur littera $O$, sequentes formae sunt notatu dignae:
I. $A+B\neq O$ existente $ABO=1$, II. $A+B+C\neq O$ existente $ABCO=1$,
III. $A+B+C+D\neq O$ existente $ABCDO=1$, etc.
Porro quia litterae $A$, $B$, $C$, $O$ sunt fractiones, si ponamus
$A=\frac{a}{b}$, $B=\frac{b}{c}$, $C=\frac{c}{d}$, etc.
sequentes habebuntur relationes impossibiles:
I. $\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}\neq\frac{c}{a}$, II. $\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{d}\neq\frac{d}{a}$, III. $\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{d}+\frac{d}{e}\neq\frac{e}{a}$.
At si hujus theorematis demonstratio haberetur, inde facile sequentia theoremata demonstrari possent:
Theorema I. Summa duorum cuborum esse nequit cubus, sive $p^3+q^3\neq r^3$.

methods.what: Reduction of Fermat's equation a^λ+b^λ=c^λ to the requirement that c^{2λ}-4d^λ be a square, with d=ab
methods.quote: ideoque pro $ab$ posito $d$, talis formula $c^{2\lambda}-4d^\lambda$ deberet esse quadratum

methods.what: Analogous square conditions derived from the same equation
Factorization of a sum of two cubes to obtain cube factors for λ=3
Parametrization c=Pp, b=Qq, a=Rr with nine resulting cubic conditions
Derived differences of the auxiliary cubes
Reformulation of the sum-times-product theorem as fractional relations via A=a/b, B=b/c, etc.

items.quote: talis formula $c^{2\lambda}-4d^\lambda$ deberet esse quadratum, cujus igitur impossibilitatem ostendi oportet, praeter casus $\lambda=1$ et $\lambda=2$.
items.english: such a formula c^{2λ}-4d^λ would have to be a square, whose impossibility must therefore be shown, except for the cases λ=1 and λ=2.

items.quote: quin etiam $a^{2\lambda}+4c^\lambda b^\lambda=\square$, quae ergo formulae etiam sunt impossibiles.
items.english: and indeed a^{2λ}+4c^λb^λ = square, which formulas are therefore also impossible.

items.english: Let a proof be attempted at least for the case λ=3 as follows

items.english: The whole matter therefore comes down to detecting a contradiction in these conditions.

items.quote: Theorema demonstrandum. Non dantur plures quantitates rationales veluti $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, etc. quarum summa $A+B+C+D$ etc. per productum $ABCD$ etc. multiplicata producat unitatem.
items.english: Theorem to be proved. There do not exist several rational quantities A, B, C, D, etc. whose sum A+B+C+D etc., multiplied by the product ABCD etc., yields unity.

items.quote:
At si hujus theorematis demonstratio haberetur, inde facile sequentia theoremata demonstrari possent:
Theorema I. Summa duorum cuborum esse nequit cubus, sive $p^3+q^3\neq r^3$.
items.english: But if a proof of this theorem were had, the following theorems could easily be proved from it: Theorem I. The sum of two cubes cannot be a cube, i.e. p^3+q^3 ≠ r^3.
